newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman to sign $2 billion gas loan in September.
newsitem.headline: Oman to sign $2 billion gas loan in September.

text.p: Oman LNG LLC will sign a $2 billion loan syndication agreement with foreign banks in September as part of the Gulf Arab state's ambitious gas-export project, a member of the firm's financing team said Monday.
"The loan documents will be signed in September under the current plan," Roderick Stead, Oman LNG LCC's financing team co-leader told Reuters.
Syndication leader U.S. Citibank will be supported by ABN-Ambro as technical adviser and National Westminister Bank Plc as global facility agent.
Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Banque Indosuez, Korea Exchange Bank and Gulf International Bank will make up the seven loan arrangers.

The loan, which will represent one of the biggest commercial loans in Middle East history, will have 27 other foreign sub-underwriting banks and export cover from the UK's ECGD, U.S. Eximbank, Dutch NCM and Italian SACE export credit agencies.
"Repayment is 8-1/2 years after completion of the (gas) plant with some basis for acceleration. There is a considerable degree of flexibility built into the loan to assist the company," Stead said.
The premium to LIBOR was confidential but was "very competitive with other Middle East projects," he added.
"There should be no need for a general syndication in view of the success of the underwriting exercise."

Up to ten local Omani banks will be approached next month to take part in the loan but their exposure will be individually limited to loans of either $5 million or $10 million based on their borrower limits.
"Apart from the documentation of the loan, the only significant exercise to complete this loan is to bring the Omani banks in," Stead said.

The $2 billion loan will be used to build a $2.5 billion, 6.6 million tonnes a year gas liquefaction plant at Qalhat in eastern Oman which will allow the first exports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) to South Korean power firms in the year 2000.
Remaining cost of the plant will be funded by equity.
A meeting in London last week between Oman LNG LLC and arranger banks extended the underwriting commitment originally signed in October 1996 which was to expire June 30.

Oman LNG had also obtained provisional credit ratings from Moody's and Standard and Poor and was examining a possible bond issue as a option to finance future investment for the project such as tankers or refinancing the project loan.
"A bond issue is under active consideration," said Stead.
Neighbouring Gulf Arab Qatar raised $1.2 billion last year in a groundbreaking bond issue for its Ras Laffan LNG project which represented the biggest project finance project in the region to date.
Oman LNG LLC is 51 percent owned by the Omani government.
Royal Dutch/Shell has 30 percent, Total SA 5.54 percent, Partex two percent, Japan's Mitsubishi Mitsui and Co 2.77 percent each and ITOCHU Corp 0.92 percent.
Under an Omami royal decree the Korean LNG Co (KOLNG) -- comprising Yukong, Hyundai, Daewoo and Samsung -- will hold the remaining five percent.
Oman is an independent, non-OPEC oil producer, pumping around 950,000 barrels per day (bpd).
